captions.detailed: A 3D-printable cylindrical knob designed with a dual-stage profile. The base consists of a wider, solid cylinder that serves as the main grip. Extending coaxially from the top of this base is a narrower, hollow shaft featuring an internal D-shaped profile with flat keyways or pins on the inside, designed to mate with a standard rotary encoder or potentiometer shaft.
captions.instruction: Design a parametric knob with a D-shaped shaft in OpenSCAD. The user should be able to adjust the top knob diameter and height, the shaft length and outer/inner diameters, and the pin width and offset inside the shaft to create a custom D-profile fit.
captions.factory: The script uses a cylinder primitive centered at the origin to define the main knob body. A second coaxial shaft is created using a difference operation between two cylinders of different diameters, translated along the Z-axis by the knob's height. To form the internal D-profile, two small rectangular cubes are calculated using trigonometric offsets (sqrt) and translated into the hollow center of the shaft to act as keyway pins.
